title: tier-2 shipped code: the per-frame vector resolve, phases 1-4, at 0x140cb2220
notes: SHIPPED-CODE tier-2 unit. The candidate is `crates/ow-sim/src/resolve.rs` (`resolve_local`, `sqrt_newton`, `rsqrtss`, `landing_rise`), called through the `mover_resolve_vector` entry of `crates/ow-sim/src/bin/verify_probe.rs`.

The oracle runs `FUN_140cb2220` (`0x140cb2220`) with `body+0x968` (the 0x40-byte record count) pinned to zero, which keeps the client out of phase 5 - both record passes sit behind `if (n40 > 0)`. That leaves phases 1-4 (properties 0x22/0x23 on the length, 0x24 on the y lane, 0x25 inside the `body+0x60c` lateral cap) and the closing landing test, which calls `MoverOnLanding` when the world lane rose by more than `0.004`.

The state file word carries bit 24 (`0x1000000`), so `0x140c9f300` and `0x140ca2740` take their direct-copy path and the stage reduces to the local law. The unit therefore proves the local law, not the transform pair.

`RSQRTSS` is what settles the square root: the oracle's value is exactly `f32(1 / f32_sqrt(x))` - 220 of 220 sampled inputs - while the double-precision forms differ in 44 of 220. `ow_sim::resolve::rsqrtss` reproduces it and `sqrt_newton` reproduces the one-Newton-step sequence, which is one ulp below the true root on `9.0` and must not be replaced by `sqrt`.
The records are the applier's input from `fn/MoverPropertyRecords`: the fixture builds them, so this unit proves the resolve, not where a record comes from.

The coverage window stops at `0x140cb24fb`, the store of the resolved vector: phases 1-4. The closing landing test at `0x140cb260e` is still compared through the body (its `MoverOnLanding` writes the flag word), but its branches are outside the window, together with phase 5's gates - those need either the bit-24-clear transform path or a matching 0x40-byte record, both outside this unit.
acknowledgedGaps: Phase 5 (the 0x40-byte record passes, mode 1 then mode 0, behind `(*body->vtable)[0xa8](body) != 2`) and its five-way plane-projection hit path at `0x140cb26a2` are not covered: the count is pinned to zero.
The transform pair `0x140c9f300`/`0x140ca2740` is not exercised: bit 24 pins the direct-copy path.
`MoverAdvance` and the swept solve - where the live position comes from - are outside this unit.

knownEquivalentMutants.why: `sq > GUARD_SQ` to `>=` differs only when `sq == GUARD_SQ` exactly, and there the inner `len > GUARD_LEN` rejects: `len = sqrt_newton(1.17549435e-36) = 1.08e-18`, three orders below the 1.19e-05 guard. The outer comparison can never change an observable.
The same argument on the masked length: at `masked == GUARD_SQ` the root is the same 1.08e-18 value and the inner guard rejects it.
